# Review: Emergency Power Sequence 3.1 to 3.5

The sequence has one critical defect: requirements 3.1 and 3.2 contradict each other, and 3.2 cannot meet the 10-second life-safety transfer. Several protective shutdowns in 3.5 could also remove power from a hospital while it is running on emergency power. I assumed NFPA 110/99 Type 10 behavior and marked it "confirm".

## Findings

| ID | Location | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| F-01 | 3.1 vs 3.2 | "Starts immediately" contradicts "after 3 s time delay". The delay uses part of the 10 s budget. | Start on the confirmed loss, or define the 10 s as measured from utility loss including SP-01. State one start trigger. |
| F-02 | 3.1, 3.2 | **Critical.** Transfer waits for both generators: confirm delay, start, stabilization (SP-05), and sync. This cannot meet SP-02. A failure of the second generator blocks life-safety power. | Transfer ATS-L and ATS-C on the first generator at the bus. Synchronize the second generator afterward. |
| F-03 | 3.2 | All three ATSs transfer at the same time, so the full inrush hits one generator. Equipment-branch loads do not need the 10 s limit. | Stage the transfers: ATS-L, then ATS-C, then ATS-E after SP-07. Add a load-acceptance check between steps. |
| F-04 | 3.2 | Stabilization delay (SP-05) sits before the second generator sync. It is unclear if it also delays the first transfer. | State that SP-05 applies only to the second generator. |
| F-05 | 3.2 | Dead-bus close has no arbitration if both generators are ready together. | Define lead-generator selection (G-1 default, operator-selectable). Add a hardwired interlock so only one generator breaker closes to a dead bus. |
| F-06 | 3.2 | Steps have no timeouts or failure responses. Sync failure, generator fail-to-start, and fail-to-close are all undefined. | Add a step table: Step, Action, Transition condition, Timeout, Failure response. |
| F-07 | 3.2 | "Rated voltage and frequency" has no thresholds. | Reference SP-04 and SP-04a. |
| F-08 | 3.3 | "Sheds load as required" cannot be tested. It gives no trigger, priority, shed order, restore rule, or latching. | List shed tiers with a cause-and-effect row for each. Shed ATS-E loads first, never ATS-L. Trigger on SP-11. Restore manually or after SP-12. |
| F-09 | 3.3 | The one-generator case covers only "available". It does not cover loss of a generator while running. | Specify a trip of one generator while loaded: immediate shed, then restore rules. |
| F-10 | 3.4 | "Immediately" retransfers on a possibly unstable utility, and the generators stop with no cooldown. The transfer type (open or closed) is not stated. | Require utility stable for SP-08. Use open or closed transition as the design decides. Run unloaded for SP-09, then stop. Re-start on a second utility loss during cooldown. |
| F-11 | 3.5 | Low fuel level should be an alarm, not a shutdown. It stops life-safety power. | Make it an alarm at SP-16, with a separate critical alarm. |
| F-12 | 3.5 | Low coolant temperature means the heater failed and the unit may start slowly. It does not justify a shutdown. | Make it an alarm only. |
| F-13 | 3.5 | High coolant temperature shutdown while carrying emergency load can drop the hospital. | Alarm at SP-13. Shut down at SP-14 only for the engine-damage case per owner and AHJ approval. Record the decision as an open item. |
| F-14 | 3.5 | Real engine protections are missing: overspeed, overcrank, low oil pressure, and electrical faults (generator protection, reverse power). | List them with trip, latch, and reset. Say which are shutdowns and which are alarms. Reference the protection relay settings. |
| F-15 | 3.5 | Shutdown behavior is undefined: which generator, latched or not, and how it resets. | Add a cause-and-effect table (cause, effect, latched or auto-reset, reset method). |
| F-16 | Whole section | Missing: bad PV (bad coolant or fuel signal), comms loss between PLC and ATS or generator controls, PLC power loss and restart, fail positions of breakers and ATSs. | Add an abnormal-handling section. The PLC must not be in the path that starts the generators or transfers ATS-L. Use local, hardwired ATS and generator control for this. |
| F-17 | Whole section | No states or modes: Standby, Starting, Island on 1 generator, Island on 2, Retransfer, Cooldown, Test, Manual, Fault. | Build the ISA-106 state and transition table first. Give permissives, initiator, and automation level. |
| F-18 | Whole section | Numbers are in prose (10 s, 3 s, 5 s). No requirement IDs or test methods. | Move values to the setpoint list. Number the requirements FR-EPS-NNN. Give each a FAT test. |
| F-19 | Whole section | Missing: weekly exercise and load-bank tests, manual and maintenance mode, operator prompts, alarms, and a retransfer-on-failure case. | Add sections for the operator interface, alarms, and testing. Reference the alarm database. |
| F-20 | 3.2 | The sentence is over 50 words and has seven actions. It breaks STE limits. | Rewrite as a step table with one action per row. |

## Provisional setpoint list

| ID | Item | Value | Units | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SP-01 | Utility loss confirm delay | 3 (as given; consider 1) | s | Confirm |
| SP-02 | Life-safety/critical transfer deadline from utility loss | 10 | s | Given |
| SP-03 | Generator start-to-ready timeout | 6 | s | Confirm |
| SP-04 | Ready voltage | 90 | % rated | Confirm |
| SP-04a | Ready frequency | 95 | % rated | Confirm |
| SP-05 | Stabilization delay before second sync | 5 | s | Given |
| SP-06 | Sync attempt timeout | 30 | s | Confirm |
| SP-07 | ATS-E delayed transfer after ATS-C | 10 | s | Confirm |
| SP-08 | Utility stable time before retransfer | 300 | s | Confirm |
| SP-09 | Generator cooldown | 300 | s | Confirm |
| SP-10 | Crank attempts / cycle length | 3 / 15 | count / s | Confirm |
| SP-11 | Single-generator shed trigger | 1350 | kW | Confirm |
| SP-12 | Load-restore stable time | 60 | s | Confirm |
| SP-13 | High coolant temperature alarm | 95 | °C | Confirm |
| SP-14 | High coolant temperature shutdown | 105 | °C | Confirm |
| SP-15 | Low coolant temperature alarm | 40 | °C | Confirm |
| SP-16 | Low fuel alarm | 24 h remaining runtime | h | Confirm |

## Corrected sequence outline (for the step table)

1. Utility loss confirmed (SP-01). Start G-1 and G-2. The local ATS and generator controls act independently of the PLC.
2. First generator reaches SP-04/SP-04a within SP-03. Close its breaker to the dead bus (F-05 arbitration).
3. Transfer ATS-L, then ATS-C, to emergency within SP-02.
4. Wait for SP-07, then transfer ATS-E, if the load check passes. If not, hold and shed per F-08.
5. After SP-05, synchronize the second generator within SP-06. On failure, alarm and stay on one generator.
6. On utility return, wait SP-08, retransfer, then cool down for SP-09 and stop.
